notes: A rear stop backing carries a 3 mm pad. Two rear-driven screws clamp it to brackets. Each bracket seats on the crossbar and has its own through bolt and nut. Each end of the crossbar now bears on 80 mm² of the side beam. Joint capacity remains open.

A spring-return pin through the NOTE bore seats in a lower socket. A closed loop ties it to the upper bridge. The raised escape test now meets 13,382 mm³ of roof; the forward displacement meets 1,455 mm³ of pin. The opening sequence retracts the pin 66 mm before discharge. Flexible-piece and latch-force measurements remain open.

Center belt uses a relieved nose and supported rear idler. The separate powered free-ring case replaces the prescribed intake animation as evidence of acquisition. No powered capture or score is credited.

At 80° a service pin indexes the rotating cassette to its truck. A 4° indexing error obstructs the pin. Battery extraction at 125° remains the retained failing case. The slide must also be restrained before hands-on service.
A rear chain saddle and telescoping guides reserve a whole endgame subsystem. Loaded attitude, holding dog and joint strength remain open. No ONSTAGE points credited.
Mass and bus voltage use design allocations. Assign staged current limits. Force, inertia, motor ratings and an actual battery discharge test are still required.

Free ring: zero-friction holds at −50, 0, 45, 90 and 125° on two numerical refinements. The maximum shift with the pin and bridge was 26.43 mm. At the two extreme angles the original open geometry allowed more than 1 metre of travel. The physical foam NOTE and latch loads still require testing.

PARK route: 10.53 s of 24 s at the declared capped speed and acceleration, against all five recorded peers. The straight approach intersects two stage legs and B2. The waypoint solution finishes at the documented Blue parking pose. Stage overhead and field occupancy remain project assumptions.
focus: Inspect Rear stop bracket to follow the load into the side beams. Play Loose NOTE to see the failed powered approach. The seated ring has positive retention.

shared.focus: Inspect the windowed panel and the shared lift crosspiece. All three sampled geometric cases are clear. A loaded single-point hang can still tip a bumper onto the floor.
notes: Windowed polycarbonate panel alone: 0.314 kg at planning density, 4.2 mm above the seated NOTE. The cover arrests outward lift but leaves an open exit along the bed. A passive flap is a separate mechanism.

Two posts connect the climb crosspiece to the cassette beams. At the 68.56 kg comparison load the peak static torque from robot weight alone is 171.2 N·m. These are geometric screens before purchasing a drive, brake and actual hook.

A finer screen covered 11,907 assumed centers of gravity. A real bumper vertex would sit 28.7 mm below the carpet at CG [-4.0, -25.0, 350.0]. Hook placement and loaded attitude require a revision before crediting a hang.
